newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Third World trade group warns WTO over mandate.
newsitem.headline: Third World trade group warns WTO over mandate.

text.p: A Third World group on trade and economic cooperation warned the World Trade Organisation (WTO) on Tuesday to deal with trade rules only, saying it had no mandate to handle labour and social issues.

The Group of 15 (G-15) said at the end of a three-day summit in Zimbabwe, that its 16 members would coordinate their policies on WTO matters and resist any attempts to widen the mandate of the global organisation.
"There seems to be such an attempt or temptation," Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe told a news conference at the closing session.
Mugabe urged the WTO to stick to issues of trade rules. "We have agreed to resist any attempts to bring labour and other social issues under the umbrella of the WTO," he said.

Third World countries, he said, were facing tremendous problems in implementing WTO agreements, and G-15 ministers would meet before, or at the WTO's first biennial ministerial conference in December in Singapore to coordinate their views.

The G-15 retains its original name although it now comprises 16 countries, namely Algeria, Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Egypt, India, Indonesia, Jamaica, Malaysia, Mexico, Nigeria, Senegal, Peru, Venezuela, Yugoslavia and Zimbabwe.
It said it was working on the admission of Kenya.
